{{Short description|Western Tacanan language of Bolivia}} {{redirect|Tacana|the Mesoamerican volcano|Volcán Tacaná|the Peruvian region|Tacna Region}} {{Infobox language | name = Tacana | fontcolor = #ffffff | nativename = | states = [[Bolivia]] | region = [[La Paz Department (Bolivia)]] | ethnicity = {{sigfig|7,350|2}} [[Tacana people]] (2012) | speakers = {{sigfig|1,150|2}} | date = 2012 | ref = e25 | familycolor = pano-tacanan | fam1 = [[Tacanan languages|Tacanan]] | fam2 = Araona–Tacanan | fam3 = Cavinena–Tacana | fam4 = Tacana Proper | nation = {{flag|Bolivia}} | iso3 = tna | glotto = taca1256 | glottorefname = Tacana }} '''Tacana''' is a Western [[Tacanan languages|Tacanan]] language spoken by some 1,800 [[Tacana people]] in [[Bolivia]] out of an ethnic population of 5,000. They live in the forest along the [[Beni River|Beni]] and [[Madre de Dios River|Madre de Dios]] rivers in the north of [[La Paz Department (Bolivia)|La Paz Department]]. Numerous dialects, now extinct, have been attributed to Tacana: Ayaychuna, Babayana, Chiliuvo, Chivamona, Idiama (Ixiama), Pamaino, Pasaramona, Saparuna, Siliama, Tumupasa (Maracani, "Tupamasa"), Uchupiamona, Yabaypura, and Yubamona.https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/hsai:vol6p157-317/vol6p157-317_mason.pdf == Phonology == === Consonants === {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" ! colspan="2" | ![[Labial consonant|Labial]] ! colspan="2" |[[Dental consonant|Dental]]/
